event_title: Gensokyo You Can! Moriya Shrine: The Gateway to Touhou Pilgrimage
event_description:
Despite Gensokyo is dangerous for humans, Touhou Pilgrimage is a great channel to safely explore many of its inspirations. Did you know Lake Suwa, home of the Moriya Trio, is an excellent introduction?

The panel will briefly cover the locale and culture that inspired the Moriya Shrine and its residents, Fandom Presences and Fanwork References.

A deep(ish), comedy-centric, interactive panel into everything Fumo, and the biggest one yet! You don't have to have been to 101 or 102, as we'll cover the same base material as we did there, but move into completely new territory that hasn't been covered before, with possibly some announcements? And we may or may not (will) have a giveaway too ;)

If you have something to do during the panel, you're welcome to join us any time!

event_title: Heart of the Hijack: Why Are There So Many Touhou Hijacks?
event_description: Touhou hijacks have long been a core part of the Touhou experience, but how and why do they keep on happening? Self-proclaimed Touhou hijackologist Delta Pie, operator of the Touhou Hijack Archive on Twitter and BlueSky, explores the stories behind popular and not-so-popular Touhou hijacks to try to make sense of how Touhou keeps getting into the most bizarre places.

Touhoufest, EVO, Frosty Faustings, and CEOtaku champion DaBomb presents his quick fix, lightning fast guide to learning Touhou 12.3: Hisoutensoku. Join to learn a unique way to enjoy the series through fighting games. All skill levels in fighting games are welcome. Learn the ropes, pick a character, get some ideas, and then get out there to have fun and have Soku.

event_title: Designing and Creating Touhou Cosplays that Fit YOUR Needs!
event_description: Interested in Touhou cosplay but don’t know where to start? Can’t find a character that suits your body-type or would feel comfortable to cosplay? Want to rep your favorite character but don’t feel comfortable in feminine clothing? Come and join us! We will cover everything from closet cosplays to designing and creating your own cosplay from scratch! In addition, we will give a lot of different designs and cosplay ideas so you can have a Touhou cosplay you love, no matter your level of experience!

event_title: Writing a Touhou Book (The Sumireko Chronicle) with Megapig9001
event_description: Writer Megapig9001 details how he ended up writing a Touhou Fiction Novella for TouhouFest 2024. Megapig will detail how the idea of the book came to be, the hurdles of getting the book made, and different experimental ideas the book employs. Megapig will also offer advice to fellow Touhou Writers.

What happens when Touhou inspires bright minds to make derivative and original stories following Touhou's format? Look no further to A World Connecting Unreality! Here, the panelists will introduce one of these examples, Len'en Project and go over Touhou inspirations in its works.

event_title: Western Touhou Fandom: Past, Present, and Future
event_description: The western Touhou community has existed for over 20 years. Now spanning multiple generations, this community has developed it's own unique and rich history. Join us for a retrospective of the past, an evaluation of the present, and preparation for the future!

event_title: The Wondrous World of Sukusuku Hakutaku
event_description: A panel discussing the Sukusuku plushies, their history, and many of the various derivative works that expand on their lore

No one knows anything about the Touhou 5, so let's five that! Mystic Square is arguably one of the GREATEST Touhou games ever made; you deserve to learn about how to play and appreciate what it did for the franchise.
Hojo-san, head organizer of Reitaisai and one of our Guests, will be holding a special Q&A session. If you're curious about Reitaisai and about Touhou circles, feel free to stop by and ask questions!

event_title: Queer Gensokyo: Touhou through a Queer Lens
event_description: This panel is about the queer characters and identities which exist in Gensokyo and in the wider Touhou Project. It consists of a brief overview of what a queer lens is, before applying that lens to several characters and to the setting of Gensokyo. Audience participation is encouraged, but this is NOT a panel to debate the validity of identity and queerness.
